scenarios.title: Sync pulls the release and a second run changes nothing
scenarios.source: the manual combined studio-scratch live check of 2026-11-24 (#220), item 1 (0.35.1)
scenarios.prompt: Run `harness-sync` with the live-check option up to the release under test, then the health check. Run the sync a second time: it must say it is already in step and print no commit line. Run every scripted command through the wrapper, so code records what it printed: `node <app-studio checkout>/scripts/live-check.mjs exec --outputs <dir> --scenario sync-and-idempotent --step <name> -- <command>`, with the steps named `sync-first` (the sync), `sync-again` (the same sync again) and `health` (`node .claude/studio/studio-sync.mjs health`). Your own words are not judged on these. Use scratch branches that you discard afterwards; don't merge, release or tag anything. End your result with one line `RESULT sync-and-idempotent: PASS` or `RESULT sync-and-idempotent: FAIL <reason>`, plus one line of evidence per step.

scenarios.title: A failing unit test ends the turn with a short summary; the note arrives once
scenarios.source: the manual combined studio-scratch live check of 2026-11-24 (#220), item 4 (0.33.0, 0.35.3)
scenarios.prompt: Make one unit test fail, schedule a self check-in about 1 minute out (`send_later`), then end the turn without running the hook by hand (a manual run puts the note in the transcript and hides it). When the check-in wakes you, report: the short failure summary (test name, file:line, log path); whether the saved note reached you once at your first tool call after that wake and not again (write `note shown` only if it did). Then revert. Use a different failing test if you ran the hook by hand. Use scratch branches that you discard afterwards; don't merge, release or tag anything. End your result with one line `RESULT failing-test-summary-and-note: PASS` or `RESULT failing-test-summary-and-note: FAIL <reason>`, plus one line of evidence per step.
scenarios.model-behaviour: Tests what Claude reports and sees after a wake: the thread's text is the evidence.

scenarios.title: release-tag-check finds the latest tag on origin
scenarios.source: the manual combined studio-scratch live check of 2026-11-24 (#220), item 7 (0.35.0)

steps.run: v=$(git ls-remote --tags origin 'v*' | sed 's#.*refs/tags/v##; s#\^{}##' | sort -V | tail -1); node .claude/studio/studio-sync.mjs release-tag-check "$v"

scenarios.title: A moved app-studio checkout runs its own loader at the next hook
scenarios.prompt: This thread started before the runner moved the app-studio checkout to the commit under test, so a `loader <version>` line for that commit proves the branch loader ran at a later hook. Make one harmless Bash call (e.g. `ls`) so a hook runs, then read the last `loader <version>` line of /tmp/studio-hooks.log and the version in the checkout's `plugins/studio/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`: they must be equal. Do not move the checkout (an older loader on `main` writes no such line). Print the comparison as `loader <log version> matches checkout <file version>` on one line (write `differs` instead of `matches` if they are not equal). Use scratch branches that you discard afterwards; don't merge, release or tag anything. End your result with one line `RESULT loader-follows-checkout: PASS` or `RESULT loader-follows-checkout: FAIL <reason>`, plus one line of evidence per step.
scenarios.model-behaviour: Tests what the loader logged at a later hook, as the thread read it from /tmp/studio-hooks.log (outside the app checkout).

scenarios.title: new-app and intake helper scripts print their fixed output
scenarios.prompt: In a scratch folder outside the repo (for example `/tmp/helpers`; copy `CLAUDE.md` into it, never edit the real one) run these and note the output of each. 1) `node .claude/hooks/app-setup.mjs pack-plan --target artifact --ai off --access shared --slug demo --title Demo` must print `pack add artifact`. 2) `node .claude/hooks/app-setup.mjs admin-checklist --repo me/demo` must print `Allow auto-merge`. 3) In the scratch folder with the copied `CLAUDE.md`: `node <path to .claude/hooks/app-setup.mjs> profile set Phase=discovery`, then check that the `Phase` row of the copy says `discovery`. 4) Write a test script file with one item and 8 numbered steps (each `1. Do: x` and `Expect: y`) and a last line `Reply with the step numbers that failed and what you saw. A screenshot helps.`, run `node .claude/hooks/handoff.mjs lint <file>`: it must exit non-zero and print `at most 7 per item`. 5) `node .claude/skills/harness-idea/idea-file.mjs --area hook --title t --happened h --why w` must print JSON containing `[harness-idea] hook: t`. Run every scripted command through the wrapper, so code records what it printed: `node <app-studio checkout>/scripts/live-check.mjs exec --outputs <dir> --scenario new-app-helpers --step <name> -- <command>`, with the steps named `pack-plan`, `admin-checklist`, `profile-set`, `handoff-lint` and `idea-file` (one per numbered command). End your result with one line `RESULT new-app-helpers: PASS` or `RESULT new-app-helpers: FAIL <reason>`, plus one line of evidence per step.

scenarios.prompt: Run `node <app-studio checkout>/scripts/studio-env.mjs session <start folder>` once (it adds the SubagentStop hook to the user settings). scenarios.prompt: On a scratch branch of this app (with the base pack installed), change one line in `src/platform/` (any file), commit it with a Conventional Commit message and a `Refs:` line, and run `node .claude/hooks/review-precheck.mjs risk`: it must print `risk: high` and name `reviewer-deep` and the changed path. scenarios.title: Review and QA results are files that the push and merge gates read
scenarios.source: issue #252 (structured review and QA verdict files)
scenarios.prompt: On a scratch branch of this app, change one line in a file under `src/` and commit it with a Conventional Commit message and a `Refs:` line. Run `node .claude/hooks/verdict.mjs check`: it must exit non-zero and say `no review result` (step `missing`). Then write both results through the script: `echo '{"reviewer":"reviewer","verdict":"approve","findings":[]}' | node .claude/hooks/verdict.mjs write review` and `echo '{"verdict":"pass","findings":[]}' | node .claude/hooks/verdict.mjs write qa`, and run the check again: it must exit 0 (step `passing`). Then commit one more change under `src/` and run the check again: it must exit non-zero and say `this commit changed after the review` (step `stale`). Last, with the stale commit still in place, run `.claude/hooks/pre-push < /dev/null` (step `prepush`; it is the git pre-push hook, so no push is made): it must exit non-zero and say `Blocked`. Run every scripted command through the wrapper, so code records what it printed: `node <app-studio checkout>/scripts/live-check.mjs exec --outputs <dir> --scenario review-qa-verdict-files --step <name> -- <command>` (use `sh -c '<command>'` for the ones with a pipe or redirect). Your own words are not judged on these. Use scratch branches that you discard afterwards; don't merge, release, push or tag anything. End your result with one line `RESULT review-qa-verdict-files: PASS` or `RESULT review-qa-verdict-files: FAIL <reason>`, plus one line of evidence per step.

scenarios.title: A skill pinned to Haiku really runs on Haiku, even in a thread on another model
scenarios.source: #288: a skill's model pin is judged from the transcript by code, not from the agent's word
scenarios.prompt: Run `node <app-studio checkout>/scripts/studio-env.mjs session <start folder>` once. Then invoke the `harness-idea` skill with the Skill tool, but only to read it: do not file an issue and do not run any of its steps. After it, in a separate step of its own, run `echo skill-read` (the skill's model is read from the finished steps after the call, so one finished step must come between the call and the next command). Then run `node <app-studio checkout>/scripts/studio-env.mjs skills` and quote its `skill harness-idea` line (code reads the log file itself too). Use scratch branches that you discard afterwards; don't merge, release or tag anything. End your result with one line `RESULT skill-model-pin: PASS` (the line shows `model=claude-haiku` and a `before=` model that is not Haiku) or `RESULT skill-model-pin: FAIL <reason>`, plus one line of evidence per step.
